searchText: <@!395438948488445973> There's a bit better spec here: https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/blob/master/json-rpc/spec.json It still does not define the behavior but rather the interface Per the 1559 wallet call, there was a desire for `eth_gasPrice` to be backwards compatible so initial thought is to add a new optional parameter that signals the caller would like to receive a 1559-style estimate. The alternative is we could add new endpoints `eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas` and `eth_maxFeePerGas` that clients can call to get the new info. cc: <@!322222239850168331> Either way, we need to maintain the current functionality of the GPO within the nodes for those using legacy transactions Good with either 🙂 The one concern was that we’re basically versioning an inversioned api. I’m looking for failure mode... I’ve taken some test suites off GitHub for both truffle and hardhat and my project had tests not passing. Those tests were expecting failure (reverted) and were not failing with the embedded EVM, so I wiresharked the embedded one to see what it was doing and learned about some convention with an error object in the response containing message and data properties. I also then found it discussed in GitHub issues of go-ethereum.
